questions.q: 'Each of the students ___ (has/have) submitted the form.'
questions.a: 'has' — 'each' is always singular. A wrong answer 'have' is semantic plurality: many students pictured, but 'each' singles them out grammatically.

questions.q: 'Neither the teacher nor the students ___ (was/were) ready.'
questions.a: 'were' — the nearer subject 'students' governs. A wrong answer 'was' either reverses the proximity rule or treats 'neither' as the subject.
'has' — 'some' takes its number from 'water' (uncountable). A wrong answer 'have' treats 'some' as inherently plural.

questions.q: Class 9 concord adds the ______ pronouns to the head-noun rule: each/every/everyone/nobody are always singular; few/many/several always plural; some/all/most take their number from the of-phrase.

Fill in the blank: Class 9 concord adds the ______ pronouns to the head-noun rule: each/every/everyone/nobody are always singular; few/many/several always plural; some/all/most take their number from the of-phrase. 'Neither…nor' agrees with the NEARER subject.
Fill in the blank: The three-box sort: ALWAYS ______ (each, every, everyone, everybody, someone, nobody, either, neither alone).
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student applies head-noun agreement through decoy phrases, assigns fixed number to indefinites, resolves neither/either-or proximity, and handles collective nouns by the unit/members test.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: The three-box sort: ALWAYS SINGULAR (each, every, everyone, ______, someone, nobody, either, neither alone).
